  ```python
  def build_search_url(language):
      q = "created:>2023-01-01"
      url = f"https://api.github.com/search/repositories?q={q}&sort=stars&order=desc"
      if language:
          url += f"&q=language:{language}"
      return url
  ```

  The GitHub Search API uses a single `q` query parameter. The `q` parameter supports multiple qualifiers combined in a single string. 

  When `language` is provided, the code appends `&q=language:{language}`, which adds a **second** `q` parameter. The GitHub API will only recognize the first `q` parameter (or the last, or combine them unpredictably — but in standard URL parsing, duplicate parameters often result in only one being used). 

  The correct approach would be to include the language qualifier in the existing `q` parameter: `q=created:>2023-01-01+language:{language}`.

  So the bug is: when `language` is provided, a second `q` parameter is appended to the URL with `&q=`, instead of appending the language qualifier to the existing `q` parameter value. The GitHub API expects a single `q` parameter with space-separated qualifiers (URL-encoded as `+`), so the second `q` parameter will be ignored, effectively filtering by language being silently dropped.
